text: If AI keeps evolving,would you worry about your next generation's survival | Hacker News Hacker News new | past | comments | ask | show | jobs | submit login If AI keeps evolving,would you worry about your next generation's survival 8 points by hanstyle 2 hours ago | hide | past | favorite | 4 comments Imagine this. Twenty years from now, if AI is capable of handling all work, how will your kids make ends meet? If you want to prevent that future, what should you be doing today? riffraff 1 hour ago | next [–] Mildly worried. But I think most of what is useful today to teach children (to be independent, persistent, empathetic, thoughtful, etc) will still be useful in whatever future we end up in. I think even skills that may be obsolete will probably be good for training their brain, like, perhaps speaking more languages won't help because we'll all have star-trek-like communicators, but the mental flexibility won't be wasted. I'm not sure what will happen with higher studies, my kids are small. Maybe they'll study something and by the end of university there won't be a job market for it. But that could always happen, and some paths always had more career opportunities or less. Beyond education, I try to save some money (invest in some global index fund) and hopefully that will help. I was always going to do that anyway, it just feels a bit more necessary now. reply Lio 23 minutes ago | prev | next [–] It’s just another “don’t look up” issue. We’ve known about global warming for years and ignored it. People know and still buy bigger cars every year. Pick up trucks are so huge now you can’t see the child you’re about to run over and they sell like hot cakes. In surveys truck owners say they only care about occupant safety. They know about the issue for pedestrians, they just don’t care. Same with shifting industrial production and jobs to China. We know these things are problems for the next generation. When it comes to purchases people don’t care.
